card.name: We and us in shared-group statements
card.fires_on: First-person plural words such as us, we, our and actions, mostly in speeches, quotes and religious or moral writing where a group speaks about itself. Often follows let or sits inside a phrase about what we must do.

modes.label: Let us
modes.description: The word us right after let in an exhortation.
modes.example: With their blood let<< us>> create mankind.

modes.label: We as subject
modes.description: The word we starting a clause about a group's shared action or experience.
modes.example: That is the faith<< we>> must yield to the maidens' consent

modes.label: Our-phrases
modes.description: A noun or word following our that refers to shared effort.
modes.example: Our first<< step>> is to develop a simple framework with placeholders

card.writes: It seems to push away group-unity words like together and ourselves, and favors other-language or second-person words.
card.plain: It lights up on we, us and our when a group speaks about what it will or must do together.
